# applies them, W landing only with C; --without <rung> leaves that rung out of the block, should one be dropped before
# the launch, and refuses to leave out C while W stays, since W lands only with C. A rung's section runs from its
# heading to the next ### heading, as check23.js reads it.
# Generates the MANIFEST block (CLIMB-BATCH-23.md) for the batch workflow
# (explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js; explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/batch-redesign.md)
# from the record and the briefings of lists23.py, into $OUT23/manifest23.js ($FORTRESS_HOME/tmp by default, which is
# ignored); check23.js checks it and splices it. On batch 15's pattern (plan-15/manifest/gen15.py): each rung's
# section of the record's section 3 goes into the block word for word as the rung's section, which every role on the
# rung reads (the worker, the skeptic, a judge and a repair round), its code-span backticks dropped and any ellipsis
# character written as three full stops, since the script carries ASCII only; the briefing's reasons go beside the
# keys, and the script renders them at the end of the worker's brief; the manifest fields (slug, worktree, expected
# minutes, the stage as the test, the step a rung brings into the gate, the checker count a rung declares, the rungs
# it lands only with, the blurb and the points to report) come from the record's section 5, "The manifest, rung by
# rung", and the intro every agent reads from its "What every agent reads first". No value is set at launch: the
# gather numbers the batch's new rows through ledger.py, so the block has no LEDGER_FROM. No rung declares a checker
# count; W lands only with C.
#   python3 -B gen23.py [--without <rung>] [RECORD]      RECORD defaults to explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-23.md
import json, re, sys, os
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
from lists23 import LISTS, REASONS, IDS as ALL_IDS

ROOT = os.environ.get('FORTRESS_HOME', os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, '../../../..')))
argv = sys.argv[1:]
WITHOUT = []
while '--without' in argv:
    WITHOUT.append(argv[argv.index('--without') + 1])
    del argv[argv.index('--without'):argv.index('--without') + 2]
args = [a for a in argv if not a.startswith('--')]
assert all(w in ALL_IDS for w in WITHOUT), ('--without names a rung not in the batch', WITHOUT)
assert not ('C' in WITHOUT and 'W' not in WITHOUT), ('W lands only with C: --without C needs --without W too', WITHOUT)
IDS = tuple(r for r in ALL_IDS if r not in WITHOUT)
BATCH = '23'
REC = args[0] if args else os.path.join(ROOT, 'explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-23.md')
OUT = os.path.join(os.environ.get('OUT23', os.path.join(ROOT, 'tmp')), 'manifest%s.js' % BATCH)
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT), exist_ok=True)
rec = open(REC, encoding='utf-8').read()


def ascii_text(t):
    t = t.replace('`', '').replace('…', '...')
    bad = [c for c in t if ord(c) > 127]
    assert not bad, ('non-ASCII left', bad, t[:120])
    return t


def between(text, start, end):
    i = text.index(start)
    j = text.index(end, i + len(start))
    return text[i + len(start):j]


# Section 3: one block per rung, from its heading to the next ### heading.
s3 = between(rec, '\n## 3. The rungs\n', '\n## 4. ')
heads = list(re.finditer(r'^### ([A-Z])\. (.*)$', s3, flags=re.M))
assert [h.group(1) for h in heads] == list(ALL_IDS), [h.group(1) for h in heads]
sections, titles = {}, {}
for i, h in enumerate(heads):
    rid = h.group(1)
    if rid not in IDS:
        continue
    nxt = re.search(r'^### ', s3[h.end():], flags=re.M)
    end = h.end() + nxt.start() if nxt else len(s3)
    body = s3[h.end():end].strip('\n')
    assert body.startswith('**The answers this rung follows.**'), rid
    sections[rid] = ascii_text(body)
    titles[rid] = ascii_text(h.group(2))

# Section 5: the manifest fields, rung by rung, and the intro.
s5 = rec[rec.index('\n## 5. How it is run\n'):]
mrung = between(s5, '\n### The manifest, rung by rung\n', '\n### What every agent reads first\n')
blocks = list(re.finditer(r'^#### ([A-Z])$', mrung, flags=re.M))
assert [b.group(1) for b in blocks] == list(ALL_IDS), [b.group(1) for b in blocks]
FIELDS = {}
for i, b in enumerate(blocks):
    rid = b.group(1)
    if rid not in IDS:
        continue
    text = mrung[b.end():blocks[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(blocks) else len(mrung)]
    f, points, in_points = {}, [], False
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        m = re.match(r'^- \*\*([a-z ]+):\*\*\s*(.*)$', line)
        if m:
            key, val = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()
            in_points = (key == 'points to report')
            if not in_points:
                f[key] = ascii_text(val)
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^  - (.*)$', line)
        if m and in_points:
            points.append(ascii_text(m.group(1).strip()))
    f['points'] = points
    for k in ('slug', 'worktree', 'expected minutes', 'its test is the stage', 'writes state', 'joins the gate', 'checker count', 'lands only with', 'blurb'):
        assert k in f, (rid, k)
    assert points, (rid, 'no points to report')
    FIELDS[rid] = f
intro = between(s5, '\n### What every agent reads first\n', '\n### Before the launch\n').strip()
INTRO = ascii_text(intro)

def yes(v):
    assert v in ('yes', 'no'), v
    return v == 'yes'

def js(x):
    return json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=True)

def js_list(keys, indent='      '):
    out, cur = [], ''
    for k in keys:
        piece = js(k)
        if cur and len(cur) + len(piece) + 2 > 150:
            out.append(indent + cur.rstrip())
            cur = ''
        cur += piece + ', '
    if cur:
        out.append(indent + cur.rstrip().rstrip(','))
    return '\n'.join(out)

L = []
A = L.append
A('// ===========================================================================')
A('// MANIFEST - the coordinator replaces everything between this line and the')
A('// "END MANIFEST" line, and changes nothing else in this file.')
A('//')
A('// Generated by explorations/compile-ladder/plan-23/manifest/gen23.py from')
A('// CLIMB-BATCH-23.md (section 3, each rung\'s section word for word; section 5, the')
A('// manifest fields and the intro) and the briefings of lists23.py; check23.js checks it.')
A('// Climb batch 23: rungs C, W, in the order the gather applies them; W lands only with C.' + (' This block leaves out ' + ', '.join(WITHOUT) + '.' if WITHOUT else ''))
A('// Per rung: id, slug, path, branch, expectedMinutes (the scatter\'s start order only),')
A('// writesState, testIsStage, gateJoins (a gate step the rung brings), blurb (one line')
A('// for the batch table), section (the rung\'s section of the record, read by every role')
A('// on the rung), pointsToReport, briefing and reasons (the facts-extract.sh keys the')
A('// worker reads first, each with its reason), checks (the sub-list the skeptic, a judge')
A('// and a repair round read), expectedMoves (ladder moves declared, none here), and the')
A('// optional landsOnlyWith, expectedCheckerCount and expectedCheckerCrash: W lands only')
A('// with C, and no rung declares a checker count or a crash (the count is reported).')
A('// No value is set at launch. The base and the base build are args.base and')
A('// args.baseBuild. At most two agents run at once on this box, FIFO (FACTS.md, "The')
A('// Workflow harness runs two agents at once on this box"); the scatter starts the')
A('// longest expected worker first.')
A('// ===========================================================================')
A('')
A("const BATCH = '%s'" % BATCH)
A("const BATCH_RECORD = 'explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-23.md'")
A("const BRIEFING_LISTS = 'explorations/compile-ladder/plan-23/manifest/lists23.py'")
A('')
for rid in IDS:
    A('const %s_SECTION = [' % rid)
    for l in sections[rid].split('\n'):
        A(js(l) + ',')
    A("].join('\\n')")
    A('')
for rid in IDS:
    f = FIELDS[rid]
    b, c = LISTS[rid]
    slug = f['slug']
    assert re.fullmatch(r'[a-z0-9-]+', slug), slug
    path = f['worktree']
    assert re.fullmatch(r'/home/user/fortress-[a-z0-9-]+', path), path
    joins = [] if f['joins the gate'] == 'none' else [x.strip() for x in f['joins the gate'].split(',')]
    A("const %s_ENTRY = { id: '%s', slug: '%s', path: '%s', branch: 'wip/%s', expectedMinutes: %d," % (rid, rid, slug, path, slug, int(f['expected minutes'])))
    cc = f['checker count']
    assert cc == 'none' or re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+', cc), (rid, cc)
    low = f['lands only with']
    lw = [] if low == 'none' else [x.strip() for x in low.split(',')]
    assert all(x in ALL_IDS and x != rid for x in lw), (rid, low)
    assert all(x in IDS for x in lw), (rid, 'lands only with a rung this block leaves out', low)
    A('    writesState: %s, testIsStage: %s, gateJoins: %s, expectedMoves: [],%s%s' % ('true' if yes(f['writes state']) else 'false', 'true' if yes(f['its test is the stage']) else 'false', js(joins), '' if cc == 'none' else ' expectedCheckerCount: %d,' % int(cc), '' if not lw else ' landsOnlyWith: %s,' % js(lw)))
    A('    title: ' + js(titles[rid]) + ',')
    A('    blurb: ' + js(f['blurb']) + ',')
    A('    section: %s_SECTION,' % rid)
    A('    pointsToReport: [')
    for p in f['points']:
        A('      ' + js(p) + ',')
    A('    ],')
    A('    briefing: [')
    A(js_list(b) + '],')
    A('    reasons: [')
    for k, r in REASONS[rid]:
        A('      ' + js(ascii_text(r)) + ',')
    A('    ],')
    A('    checks: [')
    A(js_list(c) + '] }')
    A('')
A('const RUNGS = [' + ', '.join('%s_ENTRY' % r for r in IDS) + ']')
A('const BATCH_INTRO = ' + js(INTRO))
BLOCK = '\n'.join(L) + '\n'
for line in L:
    assert all(ord(c) < 128 for c in line) and '`' not in line, line[:120]
open(OUT, 'w').write(BLOCK)
print('batch', BATCH, 'wrote', OUT, len(L), 'lines')
for rid in IDS:

<!-- The probes of climb batch 23's planner (CLIMB-BATCH-23.md, section 4, "The planner's probes", holds their results): what each file here is, the tree it was measured on, and how to run it again. Written 2026-10-24 by an Opus planning worker against main at e0ec620a9, whose code is 2bff2fe23's, climb batch 22's landing; re-checked 2026-10-30 against the new base, a1f8c4b8b, whose code is that of main after climb batch 22c's landing (b81d86b75). -->

# Climb batch 23's probes

All runs were in three worktrees seeded from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base23` (`e0ec620a9`), detached and removed after: `fortress-p23w`, `fortress-p23c` and `fortress-p23b`. The base build ran only `count.sh` (javap on its build, which writes nothing there), `git apply --check` of the two patches, and `run-four.sh` with its scratch folder outside it; `git status --porcelain` there printed nothing after each. Machine: nproc 4, Intel Xeon Processor @ 2.10 GHz, openjdk 25.0.4.1, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` for the stages; another probe worker shared the machine, so no time here is one to compare, and walk was not timed.

The re-check of 2026-10-30, on the new base `a1f8c4b8b`: two worktrees seeded detached from the base build, now at that commit, and removed after: `fortress-p23f`, the base, for `count.sh`, `run-four.sh` and the old code, and `fortress-p23r`, the two patches applied. Nothing was built or run in the base build. The record's section 4, "The planner's probes", "On the new base", holds its results.

## The files

- `rung-C.patch`: rung C's text as the planner measured it. `compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java` (new, 134 lines, item 35's probe class re-based with three changes: its switch, the refusal of a helper string that names no static method, and `namesHelpers`), two hooks in `compiler/Parser.java` (+5 −2), the switch in `Shell.specificRepository` (+2), a reading of the foreign Java types as the one library's in walk's world in `compiler/NamingCzar.java` (+45), beside the prelude's table, and three compiled tests in `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/`. Applies to the base alone, at `e0ec620a9` and at `a1f8c4b8b`. Natives-shape's gap 1 patch from `4a46fb83a`, which the planner first applied in its place (+14 −11), rewrote the table every reading shares and failed `NamingCzarJUTest.testForeign` in the compiled tracks; the record's section 4 gives both runs.
- `rung-W.patch`: rung W's text as the planner measured it. `interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java` (new, 208 lines), its hook in `interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java` (+8), the first family's 21 strings (19 of `ZZ32`'s in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, 2 of `Int`'s in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`), and five walk tests in `ProjectFortress/tests/`. Applies to the base alone, at `e0ec620a9` and at `a1f8c4b8b`. The two together are the batch's text.
- `count.sh`: F-32's classes counted again on a built tree, with the natives probe's own scripts read from `4a46fb83a`; writes `classified.tsv` and `movable.tsv`. `classified-base.tsv` and `movable-base.tsv` are its output on the base, `a1f8c4b8b`, since the re-check; the planner's, on `e0ec620a9`, are those of `a6b6e9d06`, and differ from them in 11 line numbers only.
- `movable.py`: which bindings of classes A and B can name their helper as a bare string today, by the helper's Java signature read through the foreign-type table of walk's world; `count.sh` runs it.
- `family-edits.py`: moves a family of `movable.tsv` onto its helpers by exact text (`family-edits.py <tree> movable-base.tsv ZZ32,Int` wrote 23 strings; the batch's text then put `CHOOSE`'s and `Int`'s `asFloat`'s back, by hand, for the reasons in the record's section 4).
- `run-four.sh` and `four-imports-base.tsv`: the report-only check of the library components microGPT imports outside the distance: a copy of the distance stage whose component list is the one file `FOUR_TARGET` names, run once per target, and the errors it printed. Both are the re-check's: the copy is of the stage as climb batch 22c left it, setting `compile` and the fourteen, and the table its run on `a1f8c4b8b`, row for row the planner's run on `e0ec620a9` with the old stage (`a6b6e9d06`).

## How to run them again

From a worktree seeded from a base build at the batch's base (`a1f8c4b8b` since the re-check), set up as the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md` says:

    git apply explorations/compile-ladder/plan-23/probes/rung-C.patch explorations/compile-ladder/plan-23/probes/rung-W.patch
    ant compileAll        # then the library order, before the compiled tests
    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/h ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelper*Walk.* ProjectFortress/tests/ZZ32DivisionByZeroWalk.fss
    ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh c23 ProjectFortress/compiler_tests NativeHelperBindingCompiled.test XXXNativeHelperMisfitCompiled.test XXXNativeHelperMisspeltCompiled.test
    explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh tmp/distance.txt tmp/distance        # in the background
    explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh tmp/count.txt tmp/count         # in the background

and for the count, from any built tree: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-23/probes/count.sh <tree> <out-dir>`.
#!/bin/bash
# count.sh <built tree> <out-dir>: F-32's classes counted again on a tree (climb batch 23's planner).
# The count scripts of the natives probe (perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape/count/, read from 4a46fb83a, where they
# left the tree in fc89ee7a5) run unchanged on the tree's library: extract.py lists every live builtinPrimitive binding
# of the nine native files, match.py matches each against the compiler prelude's import-java bodies, classify.py sorts
# them into A (the prelude binds the same operation at the same owner and signature), B (a helper exists), C (a new
# helper needed), D1 (a native I/O object) and D2 (no compiled analogue). The helpers' signatures are read again with
# javap from the tree's build (ProjectFortress/build/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/), constructors left out, in the
# probe's helpers-javap.txt form. Then movable.py, beside this script, marks each A or B binding whose helper's Java
# signature, read through the foreign-type table as walk's world reads it (int ZZ32, long ZZ64, double RR64, float
# RR32, boolean Boolean, String String, BigInteger ZZ, void (), the six special-name helpers NN32, NN64 or Char), fits
# the declaration with self first: the bindings whose string can name the helper as it stands. Writes
# <out-dir>/classified.tsv, movable.tsv and helpers-javap.txt; builds and runs no Fortress.
set -eu
T=$(cd "$1" && pwd); O=$(mkdir -p "$2" && cd "$2" && pwd)
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
for f in extract.py match.py classify.py; do
  git -C "$T" show 4a46fb83a:explorations/perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape/count/$f > "$O/$f"
done
( cd "$T/ProjectFortress/build" && for c in com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/*.class; do
    n=$(basename "$c" .class); case $n in *'$'*) continue ;; esac
    javap -p -cp . "com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.$n" | grep -E '^\s+(public|private|protected|static).*\(' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/com\.sun\.fortress\.nativeHelpers\.//g' | while read -r l; do printf '%s\t%s\n' "$n" "$l"; done
  done ) | awk -F'\t' '{ if ($2 ~ ("^(public|private|protected) " $1 "\\(")) next; print }' > "$O/helpers-javap.txt"
mkdir -p "$O/run"; cp "$O"/extract.py "$O"/match.py "$O"/classify.py "$O/run/"
( cd "$T" && python3 -B "$O/extract.py" "$O/run" )
( cd "$O/run" && python3 -B match.py && python3 -B classify.py )
cp "$O/run/classified.tsv" "$O/classified.tsv"
python3 -B "$HERE/movable.py" "$O/classified.tsv" "$O/helpers-javap.txt" > "$O/movable.tsv"
